brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb (centre plus six around it)
requirements.evidence: 7 full bases: the centre at 0,0 and the six around it, joined by 12 joint bolts.

requirements.requirement: Covered on top to form a work surface
requirements.evidence: 7 top covers, one on each base, sit flush with each other.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 18 solid caps, and the check lists no open edges (no OPEN_CAP_FACE).

finish.summary: I built the seven-cell honeycomb work surface as asked. A centre full hex base has six more full bases around it. All seven have a top cover, so together they make one flush surface. 18 solid end caps finish every open outside edge, and 12 joint bolts lock the joints so the cells can't slide apart. That comes to 53 parts, about 2,728 g of filament and 4,010 minutes of printing. The final check found no rule issues and no parts colliding. The configurator only checks fit, so it says nothing about how much weight the surface can carry.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
